title: SIP vs Lump Sum: The Decision Tree for Mumbai Investors
summary: A simple framework to choose between SIP and lump sum
metaDescription: When to use SIP vs lump sum? A clear decision tree for Mumbai investors based on amount, market conditions, and psychology.
author: BM Wealth Editorial Team
tldr: If amount < 3 months salary: Lump sum. If amount > 6 months salary: STP or phased. If monthly surplus: SIP. Psychology matters more than math for most investors.

title: Property vs SIP in Mumbai: The ₹1.5Cr Decision

metaDescription: Should you buy property in Mumbai or invest in SIPs? A detailed comparison with real numbers, opportunity costs, and decision framework.
author: BM Wealth Editorial Team
tldr: At ₹1.5Cr with 5% property growth and 12% equity CAGR, the SIP route shows ₹90L more wealth in 15 years. But property has utility value and forced savings. Decision depends on your goals.

title: Lawyer's Fine Print: Nominee ≠ Owner
summary: A legal expert explains why nominations don't transfer ownership
metaDescription: Your MF nominee is not the owner. A lawyer explains the difference between nomination and succession, and why your will matters.
author: Adv. Rahul Mehta (Guest)
tldr: Nominee is a custodian, not owner. Without a will, succession laws apply and assets may not go where you intended. Simple fix: Make a will, update it yearly.
